answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging every new identity a refundable stake bond locked for several epochs, like planting an orchard where each tree must survive seasons before it bears fruit. A flood of fake accounts is an ocean of cheap identities, but each one must lock real capital, so spawning thousands costs thousands of bonds. Random peer audits slash bonds of identities whose work fails verification, turning mass creation from free into ruinously expensive while honest agents keep their velvet-smooth access.
